sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He has not committed any offence as claimed by prosecution.

The contents reported in F.I.R. is a civil dispute between the parties and giving the colour of criminal prosecution, an F.I.R.
has been lodged by informant.

According to the prosecution story, a tripartite agreement has been executed for mining work between opposite party No. 2 and the applicant who was functioning as attorney of one Shri Balveer Singh S/o Dharm Singh in favour of whom, a mining lease was executed by competent authority.
Initially, lease deed was executed in favour of Kartar S/o Santhlal for mining on 29.03.2014.
After the death of Kartara Singh, lease was transferred in favour of Kallu S/o of Kartara Singh which was valid up to 16.06.2023.
Kallu transferred all the right to one Balbeer Singh who in turn executed power of attorney in favour of Suresh Kumar Pundir.
Applicant and informant entered into agreement which is filed as Annexure No. 5 along with bail application.

According to the agreement, second party i.e. present applicant, while providing all the required assistance to the first party for the sale of dug-out product in the market available for this product because the second party has prior experience and the first party was to provide capital to set-up the business in respect of which first party will be entitled to get 70 per cent share of business revenue.
The account of mining was to be managed by the first party and second party has to obtain all the pending/permissions clearances from the respective authorities of the department.
It is also entailed in agreement that if there is dispute between the parties, the differences shall be referred to arbitration.

It is further submitted that informant without preferring the matter to the arbitration as is required as per agreement, had given the false colour of criminality and lodged this F.I.R. against the applicant.
It is further submitted that by no stretch of imagination, the dispute can be termed as ciminal as all the parties derived their rights and duties in the light of agreement executed between them.
4. It is further submitted that during the course of investigation, applicant had approached to this Court by filing Misc. Writ Petition No. 13739 of 2021.
The stay order was passed by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court.

Applicant had paid much more money to Kallu S/o of Kartar Singh, in compliance of the agreement and applicant has no knowledge regarding the termination of power of attorney executed by Kallu in his favour.

It is also submitted that the allegation with regard to submitting false and forged documents with certain Government departments for obtaining the permissions are false and concocted as there is no complaint on behalf of any department against the present applicant for obtaining permission on the basis of false or fabricated documents.
It is also submitted that informant instead of paying capital, as per agreement, lodged this F.I.R. against him in order to harass him.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant, Shri Nadeem Murtuza as vehemently opposed the plea of bail of the applicant on the ground that conduct of applicant, as all such account which renders him unfit to be released on bail.

An agreement between the informant and Kallu was executed on 10.02.2020 and informant had transferred 60 Lacs Rupees in the account of Firm of applicant Shiv Ganga Associate and the applicant in furtherance of conspiracy concealed the agreement that had taken place between Kallu and informant.

It is also submitted by learned counsel for the informant that on being contacted to the owner of land-Kallu he was informed that after the agreement executed between the parties, the power of attorney could only be executed by Kallu, hence finding the suspicious activity of applicant, he got the same cancelled on 28.09.2020.

sentences.text: At the stage of investigation also, there was no co-operation by the applicant.
It is also submitted on behalf of the informant that during pendency of another bail application, his account was freezed during disposal of another bail application.

The applicant moved an application that he want to repay the amount to informant but he is not in position to repay as his account has been freezed by the Bank and when the co-ordinate Bench of this Court found that the forged order of Bank is filed to show that the bank account is freezed, then the Court sent a letter to Bank regarding the amount deposited in such account number.
Very meager amount was found in the account which was not sufficient to discharge the burden of applicant.

It is also submitted that applicant has criminal antecedents and if accused is released on bail there will not be any possibility to settle the dispute and the applicant shall not co-operate with the trial.
6. Learned AGA also opposed the bail application on the ground that applicant has committed a crime involving about 60 lacs Rupees.
7.

Learned counsel for the applicant by way of supplementary affidavit submitted that in contempt petition No. 8 of 2022, co-accused Balbeer Singh Pundir has already been discharged by the Court on 16.10.2023 on ground that inadvertently wrong bank account number was typed in the affidavit.

On this point also, learned counsel for the informant submitted that in contempt petition also,
Balbeer Singh was discharged on the ground that he had no active role in submission of forged documents before the Hon?ble Court as it is evident from the record that the forged documents is in respect of respondent No. 1 and not in respect of respondent No. 2 and inspite of the fact he had given his unconditional apology in Court.

It is further submitted that contempt proceedings against respondent No. 1 i.e. present applicant remained operative, hence, it is submitted that drop of contempt proceedings against co-accused Balbeer are not operative against the applicant, he cannot derive any benefits from that order.
8. I have heard the rival submissions advanced on behalf of the parties and perused the entire material brought on record.
9. It is apparent that there was an agreement for mining operation on the land of Kallu S/o of Kartara between Kallu and Balbeer.
Balbeer executed power of attorney in favour of present applicant.
The investment of money was to be made by the informant and the permission etc was to be obtained by present applicant.

It was also agreed that if any defect occurred in the execution of license or it is cancelled, the applicant shall be responsible to return the invested money to the informant with an interest of 18 percent.
Payment schedule is also stated in paragraph No. 12.

First installment of capital was released by informant in favour of applicant?s company (Shiv Ganga Associate) and in the meantime, the dispute arose between the parties regarding the payment of money and allegation and counter allegations were levelled against each other.
It is also evident from the record that applicant did not co-operate during trial and contempt proceedings were drawn against him which are still pending in the Court of competent jurisdiction.

There is no indication in the application for bail whether the applicant contemnor appeared in contempt petition so far or not, but, if the applicant has committed any default in appearing before the Contempt Court,
Contempt Court is competent to take action against applicant.

3 informant to the applicant there is arbitration clause in the agreement to the effect that if there is dispute of money that can be referred to arbitration, charge-sheet has already been filed.
There is no document on record which is alleged to be forged or fabricated.
Moreover, the applicant has to obtain sanction and payments as per agreement.
It is contention of informant that he did not inform him about the sanction or communication with the Government Departments that constitute no offence at this stage.
Charge-sheet has already been filed, hence, no fruitful purpose is to be solved by detaining the applicant in jail as he is already languishing in jail since 18.10.2022.

There is criminal history of present applicant also, which is explained in paragraph No. 37 and he has been enlarged on bail in case crime No. 305 of 2021 and another case is under Section 2/3 of Uttar Pradesh Prevention of Gangsters and Antisocial Activities Act, hence, criminal history is well explained.

sentences.text: However, looking into the conduct of applicant, heavy surety is required to be executed by him.
10. Keeping in view all the facts and circumstances, applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, bail application is allowed.

11. Let applicant Suresh Kumar Tanwar be released on bail in the above case crime number and on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties of Rs. 2,00,000/- each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

(v) The applicant shall also furnish an undertaking from the sureties that the properties (movable/immovable) which are the basis of accepting the surety, shall Suresh Kumar Tanwar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 16 January, 2024
